turns.text: Current activity context: the user has a spreadsheet named Q3-Forecast.xlsx open with unsaved edits to the revenue tab, an unread email from the finance lead titled 'Forecast sign-off needed by Thursday', and a calendar block tomorrow at 10am called 'Q3 Planning'. Propose the three most useful next actions, ordered by urgency. For each, give a one-line rationale. Do not ask questions.
Keep only the most urgent one of the three you just proposed and expand it into a checklist of at most five concrete steps.
The finance lead just replied that the deadline moved to next Tuesday. Re-rank your original three actions given this change and state in one sentence what becomes the new top priority.
The user now has 10 minutes before a call. In one sentence, what should they do right now based on everything above?
Draft a professional email to a supplier escalating a repeated delivery delay and requesting a written remediation plan within five business days, while preserving the relationship.
Make it noticeably firmer without becoming rude, and cut it to under 120 words.
Add one sentence proposing a 15-minute call on Thursday, and change the remediation deadline to three business days. Return the full email.
Now write the one-line subject for that email and a two-sentence summary the user can paste into their team chat.

The user was away for three days. Produce a prioritized catch-up digest from the following. Group by what needs a decision, what needs a reply, and what is FYI only.

- Finance lead emailed twice asking for Q3 forecast sign-off, deadline Thursday.
- The tablet refresh was postponed to next quarter; product lead owes a revised launch plan by month end.
- A supply chain delay is affecting two product lines.
- Headcount grew by 40 people; IT is asking about laptop provisioning capacity.
- A customer escalation about display flicker at 120Hz was resolved by a firmware rollback.
- Someone reshared last quarter's all-hands recording.
- The office is changing its coffee vendor.
For the items you placed under 'needs a decision', list the specific decision the user must make and what information they still lack.
Draft a three-sentence reply to the finance lead that acknowledges both emails and commits to a sign-off time, consistent with the digest.
Condense the entire catch-up into one sentence for a status update to the user's manager.

Here is a transcript of a meeting the user attended. Capture the key points, decisions and owners.

'Okay so on the display flicker issue, we rolled back the fan firmware on the affected units and nine of eleven are stable now. Maria, can you own tracking the remaining two? Yes. Good. Second thing, the tablet refresh slips a quarter, the panel supplier cannot guarantee volumes, Raj owns the revised plan by end of next month. And last, we need someone to audit the heatsink supplier lot, no volunteers, park it. Oh and Priya asked about laptop provisioning for the forty new hires, IT says capacity is fine through October.'
Who owns the tablet refresh plan and by when? One sentence.
Summarize the decisions from that meeting in Simplified Chinese, three bullets, for a colleague in the Beijing office.
Which item from the meeting has no owner? State it and suggest who should own it, in two sentences.

The user is sharing their screen showing a spreadsheet where cell D14 displays #DIV/0!. The formula in D14 is =C14/B14. Column B is 'units sold' and column C is 'revenue'. Explain in a conversational tone what is going wrong and what to check, as if speaking aloud.
B14 is empty because that region had no sales this month. Fix it for me: give me the exact formula to put in D14 that shows a dash instead of the error.
Now I want the same protection for the whole column D, rows 2 to 40, and I'd rather see 0 than a dash. What do I do?
Recap in one sentence what we changed and why, so I can note it in the sheet.

The user typed: 'a poster for our team offsite, mountains, morning, techy feel'. Expand this into a detailed image-generation prompt covering subject, composition, lighting, style and aspect ratio. Output only the prompt.
The user says: 'make the sky more dramatic, drop the techy feel, add our team name QIRA in the bottom right'. Rewrite the prompt you produced to reflect these edits. Output only the revised prompt.
Give me two alternative versions of that revised prompt: one photorealistic, one flat illustration. Label them A and B.
Return version B as JSON with keys: subject, composition, lighting, style, text_overlay, aspect_ratio. Output only the JSON.
